title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E420 Euler makes the 'variation' concrete. The extremal curve y(x) is embedded in a one-parameter family y(x,t), and the variation of J = ∫Z dx is its t-derivative, computed at t=0. With dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + S ds + ..., where p = y', q = y'', and so on, the previous page gave δJ = dt[∫N (∂y/∂t) dx + ∫P (∂²y/∂x∂t) dx + ∫Q (∂³y/∂x²∂t) dx + ∫R (∂⁴y/∂x³∂t) dx + ...]. Since the family is arbitrary, the quantities ∂ᵏ⁺¹y/∂xᵏ∂t have no fixed values. The 'singular artifice' announced at the end of §13 is to bring every integral to a form containing only u = ∂y/∂t.

On this page Euler notes that dx·(∂²y/∂x∂t) is the x-differential of u, with t held fixed. Integration by parts then gives ∫P u_x dx = P u − ∫P' u dx. Applying this twice gives ∫Q u_xx dx = Q u_x − Q' u + ∫Q'' u dx. Three times gives ∫R u_xxx dx = R u_xx − R' u_x + R'' u − ∫R''' u dx. Four times gives ∫S u_xxxx dx = S u_xxx − S' u_xx + S'' u_x − S''' u + ∫S'''' u dx.

§14 begins to substitute these back. The following page collects the result: δJ = dt ∫u (N − P' + Q'' − R''' + S'''' − ...) dx plus boundary terms u(P − Q' + R'' − ...) + u_x(Q − R' + ...) + .... Requiring this to vanish for every family yields the Euler–Lagrange equation for higher-order Lagrangians.
errors: None in the mathematics. All the alternating signs in the repeated integrations by parts are correct.
Minor: the integrals are indefinite, so the 'absolute parts' are evaluated without explicit limits. Euler handles them later as clausulae, i.e. boundary terms.

ideas.what: Repeated integration by parts that transfers all x-derivatives off the variation ∂y/∂t, leaving boundary terms plus a single integral against ∂y/∂t.
ideas.modern_name: Derivation of the first variation / Euler–Lagrange (Euler–Poisson) equation with boundary terms for higher-order Lagrangians
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1755 letter; Miscellanea Taurinensia 1762); Euler adopted it in E296/E297 (1766) and E420
ideas.where_published: E296 'Elementa calculi variationum', E297, E385, and Institutiones calculi integralis vol. III (appendix on variations)

ideas.what: Variation realised as the derivative with respect to an auxiliary parameter t of a one-parameter family y(x,t). Mixed partials ∂ᵏ⁺¹y/∂xᵏ∂t are treated as x-derivatives of ∂y/∂t.
ideas.modern_name: First variation as the derivative of a family (Gateaux derivative)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E420 (1772); widely noted by historians (Goldstine, Fraser)
ideas.where_published: E420 itself, and the parallel treatment in Institutiones calculi integralis III

deep.surprise_reason: This page carries out standard, well-documented integration-by-parts steps leading to the Euler–Poisson equation. The parameter method of E420 is well known in the history of the calculus of variations, and nothing here is uncredited.
